AI.result: 90.0% GKP-detection accuracy (23.7 pp improvement over baseline), fidelity MAE of 0.032, log-scale post-selection probability R²=0.837, ~90% reduction in total simulation burden.
AI.conclusion: The surrogate-driven approach makes GBS-based GKP state preparation computationally tractable by eliminating the need for exhaustive hafnian evaluations, enabling practical photonic quantum computing.

title: Polymer quantum mechanics on compact configuration spaces
summary: "Polymer quantum mechanics" is the name given to a quantization scheme inspired by loop quantum gravity in which the configuration space of the theory is chosen to have a discrete topology. Polymer quantization yields a representation of the canonical commutation relations that is genuinely distinct from the conventional "Schrödinger" representation. In this paper, we summarize the main features of polymer quantum mechanics and investigate in detail the polymer quantization of systems with configuration spaces that are classically compact. We show explicitly how using the standard construction of polymer states leads to a Hilbert space of states defined on a finite graph of points. By way of example, we find the exact energy eigenvalues and eigenfunctions for a particle on a ring and a particle in a box defined on such lattices, and discuss similarities and differences from standard Schrödinger quantum mechanics. We also explore the continuum limit of states in these systems, and demonstrate in detail how the exact eigenfunctions in the position representation approach their continuum counterparts.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses polymer quantum mechanics (inspired by loop quantum gravity), which uses a discrete configuration space topology. It focuses on quantizing systems with classically compact configuration spaces, constructing Hilbert spaces on finite graphs of points, and analyzing exact solutions for a particle on a ring and in a box, including the continuum limit.
AI.motivation: To investigate polymer quantization (a loop quantum gravity-inspired scheme with discrete topology) for systems with classically compact configuration spaces, and to understand how this alternative representation of canonical commutation relations differs from standard Schrödinger quantum mechanics.
AI.method: Polymer quantization is applied to compact configuration spaces (particle on a ring and particle in a box). Hilbert spaces are constructed on finite graphs of points (lattices). Exact energy eigenvalues and eigenfunctions are derived, and the continuum limit is analyzed by studying how these discrete eigenfunctions approach their standard Schrödinger counterparts.
AI.result: Exact energy eigenvalues and eigenfunctions for a particle on a ring and a particle in a box are obtained on finite lattices. The continuum limit is explicitly demonstrated, showing how the discrete eigenfunctions approach the standard Schrödinger continuum solutions.
AI.conclusion: Polymer quantization on compact configuration spaces yields physically sensible results that reduce to standard quantum mechanics in the continuum limit, while providing a distinctly different representation of canonical commutation relations at the discrete level.

title: Barbell Codes: qLDPC Codes for Superconducting Quantum Hardware

summary: The major challenge on the way to fault-tolerant quantum computing comes from the insufficient quality of hardware components and the difficulty of scaling their number without further compromising fidelity. Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (qLDPC) codes offer a promising solution by encoding logical qubits with low overhead and at a comparatively high code distance. However, it remains an open question how to scalably implement efficient qLDPC codes on fixed-connectivity quantum chips without increasing hardware complexity to enable the non-local interactions in their underlying QEC cycles. We resolve this challenge for the first time by introducing a family of qLDPC "barbell" codes accompanied by a realistic chip layout that natively supports all required two-qubit interactions. Crucially, the hardware complexity required to implement barbell codes remains constant as code distance increases. We provide a detailed investigation into the feasibility of all required hardware components and simulate a specific family of barbell codes against circuit-level noise. We find that, with a modest overhead of $<30$ data qubits per logical qubit, barbell codes can preserve information at a physical noise strength of $10^{-4}$ for several trillion QEC cycles. Simulations of logical multi-Pauli measurements, performed with circuits tailored to the chip, yield similar logical performance per QEC round, indicating that entangling gates between logical qubits in barbell codes can be realized fault-tolerantly.

AI.tldr: Barbell codes are a new family of qLDPC codes that natively map to fixed-connectivity quantum chips with constant hardware complexity, achieving trillion-cycle memory times with <30 data qubits per logical qubit at physical noise of 10⁻⁴.
AI.motivation: The major challenge in fault-tolerant quantum computing is insufficient hardware quality and difficulty scaling qubit count without fidelity loss. qLDPC codes promise low-overhead encoding but require non-local interactions that are hard to implement on fixed-connectivity chips without increased hardware complexity.
AI.method: The authors introduce a family of qLDPC "barbell" codes with a realistic chip layout that natively supports all required two-qubit interactions. Hardware complexity remains constant as code distance increases. They simulate barbell codes against circuit-level noise with tailored circuits for logical multi-Pauli measurements.
AI.result: With <30 data qubits per logical qubit, barbell codes preserve information at physical noise strength of 10⁻⁴ for several trillion QEC cycles. Logical multi-Pauli measurements show similar logical performance per QEC round, indicating fault-tolerant entangling gates between logical qubits.
AI.conclusion: Barbell codes resolve the challenge of scalably implementing efficient qLDPC codes on fixed-connectivity quantum chips, requiring only constant hardware complexity as code distance grows, enabling fault-tolerant logical operations.

title: Forbidden transitions in superconducting artificial atoms
summary: Artificial atoms built from Josephson junctions have become a powerful tool to explore the limits of quantum optics due to their strong coupling to electromagnetic fields and their sensitivity to changes at the single-photon level. This sensitivity to quantum fluctuations complements their metrological and computational use, which are based on the precise oscillating frequency of the underlying supercurrents. We present here a theory for Josephson junctions immersed in electromagnetic fields where focus is shifted from temporal correlations and towards spatial ones. Unlike the commonly used circuit and black-box descriptions, our work is based on a microscopic model that enables systematically accounting for the effect of the spatial and vectorial profile of an electromagnetic field over a junction. As an example of the interactions that emerge in such a setup, we investigate the possibility of driving a junction via a quadrupole transition, using typical experimental parameters in existing devices. With the transition being dependent on the gradient of the electric field -- rather than its intensity -- the junction can be excited in a region where the electric field vanishes.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a microscopic theory for Josephson junctions in electromagnetic fields, focusing on spatial rather than temporal correlations, and demonstrates the possibility of driving a junction via quadrupole transitions using the electric field gradient instead of its intensity.
AI.motivation: Existing circuit and black-box descriptions of Josephson junctions focus on temporal correlations, but fail to account for the spatial and vectorial profile of electromagnetic fields over a junction, which limits the understanding of field-matter interactions at the microscopic level.
AI.method: The authors develop a microscopic model for Josephson junctions immersed in electromagnetic fields that systematically incorporates the spatial and vectorial profile of the field, shifting focus from temporal to spatial correlations.
AI.result: The theory predicts the possibility of driving a Josephson junction via a quadrupole transition, which depends on the gradient of the electric field rather than its intensity, allowing excitation in regions where the electric field vanishes.
AI.conclusion: The spatial profile of electromagnetic fields over Josephson junctions enables new interaction mechanisms (e.g., quadrupole transitions) beyond traditional dipole-based descriptions, with implications for quantum optics, metrology, and quantum information processing.

title: Efficient Quantum Circuit Construction of Controlled Time-Evolution for Arbitrary Pauli-Sum Hamiltonians
summary: Controlled time-evolution circuits select forward or backward Hamiltonian time evolution according to the state of an ancilla qubit. They are fundamental building blocks in quantum eigenvalue transformation of unitaries, Hamiltonian filtering, and related quantum algorithms. A direct realization adds ancilla control to the elementary gates of the time-evolution circuit and therefore increases the two-qubit gate count, compiled T depth and CX depth. We develop an efficient recursive algorithm that, for an arbitrary Pauli-sum Hamiltonian, partitions the input Pauli terms into groups and assigns to each group a sign-flip Pauli string that anti-commutes with the in-group terms, thereby removing ancilla control from the grouped time-evolution blocks. Numerical benchmarks on random Hamiltonians and structured spin Hamiltonians show reductions in compiled T depth and compiled CX depth. For a Kagome Hamiltonian with 24 spins under full connectivity, the proposed construction reduces the compiled T depth by 85.2% and the compiled CX depth by 68.9%, compared with a conventional implementation that decomposes the Hamiltonian into individual Pauli terms and implements the controlled time evolution of each term by directly adding the ancilla qubit to the corresponding Pauli-rotation circuit.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a recursive algorithm to partition Pauli-sum Hamiltonians into groups with sign-flip Pauli strings that anti-commute with in-group terms, removing ancilla control from controlled time-evolution circuits. This reduces compiled T depth by 85.2% and CX depth by 68.9% on a 24-spin Kagome Hamiltonian compared to conventional direct ancilla control.
AI.motivation: Controlled time-evolution circuits are essential for quantum eigenvalue transformation, Hamiltonian filtering, and related quantum algorithms, but direct realization adds ancilla control to elementary gates, increasing two-qubit gate count, T depth, and CX depth. The paper aims to reduce this overhead.
AI.method: A recursive algorithm that partitions Pauli terms into groups and assigns each group a sign-flip Pauli string that anti-commutes with all in-group terms, thereby eliminating the need for ancilla control on grouped time-evolution blocks.
AI.result: Numerical benchmarks on random Hamiltonians and structured spin Hamiltonians show reductions in compiled T depth and CX depth. For a 24-spin Kagome Hamiltonian under full connectivity, compiled T depth reduced by 85.2% and compiled CX depth by 68.9% compared to conventional direct ancilla control implementation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed grouping and sign-flip technique significantly reduces resource overhead (T depth and CX depth) for implementing controlled time-evolution circuits, making them more efficient for quantum algorithms relying on eigenvalue transformation and Hamiltonian filtering.

title: Quantum-limited estimation of atmospheric turbulence via spatial mode decomposition
summary: We establish the ultimate precision limit for estimating the optical spatial coherence radius (Fried parameter) within a quantum metrological framework. In the weak field regime, we show that spatial-mode decomposition -- originally introduced for superresolution imaging -- enables substantially more precise estimation than conventional direct imaging when the receiver aperture is smaller than the coherence radius.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes the ultimate precision limit for estimating the Fried parameter using quantum metrology, showing that spatial-mode decomposition offers better precision than direct imaging in the weak field regime when the receiver aperture is smaller than the coherence radius.
AI.motivation: To determine the fundamental quantum limit on estimating the optical spatial coherence radius (Fried parameter) and to identify optimal measurement strategies beyond conventional direct imaging.
AI.method: Quantum metrological framework applied to the weak field regime; comparison between spatial-mode decomposition (from superresolution imaging) and conventional direct imaging for estimating the Fried parameter.
AI.result: Spatial-mode decomposition enables substantially more precise estimation than conventional direct imaging when the receiver aperture is smaller than the coherence radius.
AI.conclusion: The ultimate precision limit for estimating the Fried parameter is established, and spatial-mode decomposition is identified as a superior measurement strategy in the specified regime.

title: Deployed trusted-node quantum key distribution over 300 km with a multi-core fiber access link
summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is increasingly considered for deployment in realistic communication networks, where long distances, heterogeneous fiber infrastructure, and coexistence with classical traffic present substantial challenges. Here, we demonstrate trusted-node QKD between Linköping University and the Stockholm hub of the Swedish national quantum communication infrastructure over 270 km of deployed single-mode fiber, extended by a 33 km multi-core fiber (MCF) segment emulating a metropolitan access link, for a total distance of 303 km. The two sub-links use commercial QKD systems whose receivers are interfaced with external superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, enabling operation at losses beyond those supported by standard internal gated-mode detectors. We operate the link while actively switching the QKD channel between two MCF cores, with co-propagating Ethernet traffic and injected broadband optical noise in the other cores. The results demonstrate the integration of commercial QKD into demanding, dynamically reconfigurable fiber infrastructure relevant to future hybrid quantum-classical networks. Finally, using the generated secret keys, we illustrate how limited and time-varying QKD throughput affects one-time-pad-protected image transmission: image fidelity depends strongly on the available QKD-generated key budget and the choice of compression algorithm, highlighting application-level challenges for QKD-based encryption in realistic scenarios.

AI.tldr: Trusted-node QKD demonstrated over 303 km of deployed fiber (270 km SMF + 33 km MCF) in Sweden using commercial QKD systems with external SNSPDs, including dynamic core switching with co-propagating classical traffic, and analysis of application-level impact on one-time-pad image transmission.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate the feasibility of QKD in realistic, long-distance, deployed fiber infrastructure with coexisting classical traffic and dynamic reconfigurability, bridging the gap between lab experiments and practical network deployment.
AI.method: Used two commercial QKD systems with external superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) over a 270 km SMF link (Linköping–Stockholm) plus a 33 km MCF segment; actively switched QKD channels between MCF cores while Ethernet traffic and broadband optical noise occupied other cores; evaluated key generation and applied keys to one-time-pad image transmission.
AI.result: Successful QKD operation over 303 km total distance with active core switching and co-propagating classical traffic; image transmission fidelity depends strongly on available key budget and compression algorithm choice.
AI.conclusion: Commercial QKD can be integrated into demanding, dynamically reconfigurable fiber networks; application-level performance (e.g., image encryption) is sensitive to time-varying key throughput, highlighting challenges for real-world QKD-based encryption.

title: Semidefinite-programming hierarchies for classically simulable state families
summary: Identifying whether a state family admits an irreducible quantum advantage is a fundamental task in quantum resource theory and quantum information processing. Here we study classically simulable state families, namely those residing within the convex hull of pairwise commuting families and therefore admitting a classical explanation. We develop a complete semidefinite-programming (SDP) hierarchy characterizing the set of classically simulable state families in arbitrary finite dimension. The key step is to reformulate classical simulability as a feasibility problem over deterministic response functions and auxiliary positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) simulable by rank-one projective measurements. We establish a complete SDP hierarchy for rank-one projectively simulable POVMs and transfer the resulting characterization to state families, yielding both primal feasibility tests and dual affine witnesses certifying failure of classical simulability. Applying the hierarchy to state families mixed with depolarizing noise gives computable upper bounds on the critical classical visibility, which are matched by explicit classical simulations in several symmetric examples. These results provide a systematic convex-optimization framework for certifying classical simulability of quantum state families.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a complete semidefinite-programming (SDP) hierarchy to determine whether quantum state families are classically simulable (i.e., reside within the convex hull of pairwise commuting families). The hierarchy provides primal feasibility tests and dual affine witnesses, and yields computable upper bounds on critical classical visibility under depolarizing noise, with tight bounds in symmetric examples.
AI.motivation: Identifying whether a state family admits an irreducible quantum advantage is fundamental in quantum resource theory and quantum information processing. The authors aim to systematically certify classical simulability of quantum state families.
AI.method: The key step reformulates classical simulability as a feasibility problem over deterministic response functions and auxiliary positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) simulable by rank-one projective measurements. The authors establish a complete SDP hierarchy for rank-one projectively simulable POVMs and transfer this characterization to state families.
AI.result: The authors develop a complete SDP hierarchy yielding both primal feasibility tests and dual affine witnesses certifying failure of classical simulability. Applying the hierarchy to state families mixed with depolarizing noise gives computable upper bounds on the critical classical visibility, which are matched by explicit classical simulations in several symmetric examples.
AI.conclusion: These results provide a systematic convex-optimization framework for certifying classical simulability of quantum state families.

title: Multiple Quantum Hypothesis Testing: One-Shot Pairwise Bounds and Sharp Asymptotics

summary:
We consider Bayesian discrimination among multiple quantum states and establish a dimension-free one-shot upper bound on the minimum probability of error in terms of the sum of pairwise errors. This resolves a conjecture of Audenaert and Mosonyi [J. Math. Phys. 55 (2014)] and improves the multiple quantum Chernoff bound of Li [Ann. Statist. 44 (2016)] by removing its dimension-dependent prefactor. In the asymptotic many-copy regime, our bound proves the achievability of the multiple quantum Chernoff distance for arbitrary separable Hilbert spaces, thereby settling the previously open infinite-dimensional case, and further yields constant-factor sharp asymptotics for the optimal error probability.
  In binary quantum hypothesis testing, we prove that the minimum error probability is characterized, up to universal constants, by a trace harmonic-mean quantity. Consequently, the optimal binary quantum error probability is within a factor of two of the optimal classical error probability for the associated Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions, complementing the lower bound of Nussbaum and Szkoła [Ann. Statist. 37 (2009)].

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a dimension-free one-shot upper bound on the minimum error probability for Bayesian multi-state quantum discrimination, resolving a conjecture by Audenaert & Mosonyi and improving Li's bound by removing dimension-dependent prefactors. It proves achievability of the multiple quantum Chernoff distance for arbitrary separable Hilbert spaces and yields constant-factor sharp asymptotics. For binary quantum hypothesis testing, it shows the minimum error probability is characterized up to universal constants by a trace harmonic-mean quantity, and is within a factor of two of the optimal classical error probability for Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions.
AI.motivation: To resolve the open conjecture by Audenaert and Mosonyi regarding dimension-free bounds for multi-state quantum discrimination, and to settle the infinite-dimensional case for the multiple quantum Chernoff distance. Additionally, to characterize binary quantum error probability in terms of a trace harmonic-mean quantity and relate it to classical error bounds.
AI.method: The authors derive a dimension-free one-shot upper bound on the minimum probability of error expressed as a sum of pairwise errors, use it to prove achievability of the multiple quantum Chernoff distance for arbitrary separable Hilbert spaces, and analyze binary quantum hypothesis testing via a trace harmonic-mean characterization with universal constants.

AI.conclusion: The paper resolves the conjecture of Audenaert & Mosonyi, settles the infinite-dimensional case for the multiple quantum Chernoff distance, and provides tight characterizations for both multi-state and binary quantum hypothesis testing error probabilities.

title: Non-equilibrium thermodynamics of collapse models in the strongly non-Gaussian regime
summary: Standard objective collapse models offer a unified approach to the quantum measurement problem but predict an unphysical, indefinite increase in the energy of the system. The dissipative Diósi-Penrose (dDP) model resolves this heating issue by introducing a linear friction mechanism. However, this modification induces complex, non-Gaussian phase-space dynamics. We rigorously establish the thermodynamic consistency of this friction mechanism -- extended to the CSL model -- across both weakly and strongly non-Gaussian regimes. Using the Wigner phase-space formalism, we go significantly beyond the quadratic approximation and, to bypass the failure of perturbative methods under strong dissipation, introduce a novel exact pseudo-spectral simulation approach. Our analysis reveals that the system subjected to the dDP mechanism does not thermalize, but rather settles into a non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS) where the asymptotic non-Gaussianity scales as the third power of the dissipation parameter $β$. By evaluating the Wigner entropy production, we confirm the thermodynamic validity of the model and demonstrate that highly sensitive information-theoretic quantities require exact numerical methods to accurately capture the key non-Gaussian tails of the distribution.

AI.tldr: The dissipative Diósi-Penrose model, extended to CSL, introduces friction to resolve energy divergence but produces non-Gaussian dynamics. Using Wigner formalism and a novel exact pseudo-spectral method, the paper shows the system reaches a non-equilibrium steady state with asymptotic non-Gaussianity scaling as β³, and confirms thermodynamic consistency via Wigner entropy production.
AI.motivation: Standard objective collapse models solve the quantum measurement problem but suffer from unphysical indefinite energy increase. The dissipative Diósi-Penrose model introduces friction to fix this, but its thermodynamic consistency had not been rigorously established, especially beyond quadratic approximations and in strongly non-Gaussian regimes.
AI.method: The authors use the Wigner phase-space formalism to go beyond the quadratic approximation. To overcome the failure of perturbative methods under strong dissipation, they develop a novel exact pseudo-spectral simulation approach. They analyze the dDP model extended to the CSL model across both weakly and strongly non-Gaussian regimes.
AI.result: The system does not thermalize but settles into a non-equilibrium steady-state (NESS). The asymptotic non-Gaussianity scales as the third power of the dissipation parameter β. Thermodynamic validity is confirmed via Wigner entropy production. Exact numerical methods are required to capture key non-Gaussian tails of the distribution for sensitive information-theoretic quantities.
AI.conclusion: The dissipative Diósi-Penrose friction mechanism is thermodynamically consistent. However, the system exhibits non-equilibrium steady-state behavior rather than thermalization, and accurate characterization of non-Gaussian features demands exact numerical treatment beyond perturbative approximations.

title: Quantum Algorithms for Triangle Cut Sparsification
summary:
Triangles capture higher-order structures in graphs and are fundamental to applications such as clustering and network analysis.
  To enable efficient use of such structures at scale, we study the problem of \emph{triangle cut sparsification}, which aims to reduce the graph size while approximately preserving triangle counts across every cut.
  We investigate \emph{quantum algorithms} for this problem, using triangle listing as our main technical ingredient.
  In particular, we present a quantum algorithm for triangle listing that, for a graph with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges, and $t$ triangles, runs in time $T_{\mathrm{q\text{-}list}} =$ $\widetilde{O}\bigl(\min(n^{5/4}t^{7/12} + n^{7/6}t^{7/9}, m + m^{3/4}t^{1/2},$ $n^{3/2}t^{1/2})\bigr)$, improving upon the best known classical bounds over a broad range of parameters. Our algorithm is based on a heavy-light vertex partition and an extension of triangle detection via quantum walks and Grover search.
  Leveraging this result, we design a quantum algorithm for constructing $\varepsilon$-triangle cut sparsifiers of size $\widetilde{O}(n/\varepsilon^2)$ in time $\widetilde{O}(T_{\mathrm{q\text{-}list}} + \sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon)$.
  Finally, we demonstrate applications to clustering algorithms based on triangle-related measures
  and prove a lower bound of $Ω(n/\varepsilon^2)$ on the size of any $\varepsilon$-triangle cut sparsifiers.

AI.tldr: This paper presents quantum algorithms for triangle listing (with improved runtime over classical methods) and triangle cut sparsification, achieving sparsifiers of size \(\widetilde{O}(n/\varepsilon^2)\) with quantum speedups, and proves a matching lower bound.
AI.motivation: Triangles capture higher-order graph structures essential for clustering and network analysis, but large-scale usage requires efficient sparsification. The goal is to reduce graph size while preserving triangle counts across every cut, and to explore whether quantum algorithms can outperform classical ones for this task.
AI.method: (1) A quantum triangle listing algorithm using heavy-light vertex partitioning combined with quantum walks and Grover search, achieving runtime \(\widetilde{O}(\min(n^{5/4}t^{7/12}+n^{7/6}t^{7/9}, m+m^{3/4}t^{1/2}, n^{3/2}t^{1/2}))\). (2) Building on this, a quantum algorithm to construct \(\varepsilon\)-triangle cut sparsifiers of size \(\widetilde{O}(n/\varepsilon^2)\) in time \(\widetilde{O}(T_{\mathrm{q\text{-}list}} + \sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon)\). (3) A lower bound proof that any \(\varepsilon\)-triangle cut sparsifier requires \(\Omega(n/\varepsilon^2)\) size.
AI.result: The quantum triangle listing algorithm improves upon the best known classical bounds across a broad range of parameters. The triangle cut sparsifier construction achieves quantum speedups, and the size lower bound \(\Omega(n/\varepsilon^2)\) matches the upper bound up to polylog factors.
AI.conclusion: Quantum algorithms can provide significant speedups for triangle-based graph sparsification, with optimal sparsifier size. The results also enable efficient quantum clustering algorithms leveraging triangle-related measures.

title: Quantum enhanced rare event discovery and sampling
summary: Financial crashes, cascading failures in infrastructure, and critical errors in AI systems are frequently triggered by events that occur with extremely small probability. Efficiently discovering and sampling events with probability below a threshold is therefore of critical interest. Yet this task is highly non-trivial using existing classical or quantum methods. Being rare, such events require an immense sampling overhead to collect sufficient data samples. Moreover, because the rare events are not known in advance, they cannot be flagged for amplification using standard techniques. Here, we introduce a quantum algorithm for rare-event discovery and sampling without first learning which events are rare. The algorithm achieves the optimal quantum scaling with the rarity threshold. We further demonstrate that this can achieve a quadratic speedup for heavy-tailed systems whose tail has nonvanishing total mass, and translates into a robust polynomial speedup for stationary stochastic processes, with the exponent determined by its entropy-rate structure.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a quantum algorithm for discovering and sampling rare events (low-probability events) without prior knowledge of which events are rare, achieving optimal quantum scaling with the rarity threshold and quadratic speedup for heavy-tailed systems.
AI.motivation: Financial crashes, infrastructure cascading failures, and critical AI errors are triggered by extremely low-probability events. Efficiently discovering and sampling such rare events is critically important but highly challenging with classical or quantum methods due to immense sampling overhead and the inability to pre-identify events for amplification.
AI.method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm for rare-event discovery and sampling that does not require prior knowledge of which events are rare. The algorithm achieves optimal quantum scaling with the rarity threshold and demonstrates quadratic speedup for heavy-tailed systems with nonvanishing total tail mass, translating into a robust polynomial speedup for stationary stochastic processes with exponent determined by entropy-rate structure.
AI.result: The algorithm achieves optimal quantum scaling with the rarity threshold, quadratic speedup for heavy-tailed systems whose tail has nonvanishing total mass, and a robust polynomial speedup for stationary stochastic processes, with the exponent determined by its entropy-rate structure.
AI.conclusion: The introduced quantum algorithm efficiently solves the rare-event discovery and sampling problem without prior knowledge of rare events, achieving optimal quantum scaling and offering significant speedups over classical approaches for heavy-tailed and stationary stochastic systems.

title: Reliability of asymptotic work extraction
summary: Extracting work from quantum states is a fundamental task in quantum thermodynamics. Previous studies have primarily focused on determining the best achievable rate of work extraction, and remarkably, this characterization appeared to remain unchanged regardless of the choice of allowed processes: whether one considers the operationally motivated class of energy-conserving thermal operations, or the axiomatic class of Gibbs-preserving operations, the optimal extractable work is given by the Helmholtz free energy. Here, we challenge this perspective, showing that a more refined analysis of the asymptotic performance of work extraction reveals significant differences in the performance for the two different classes of free operations. Precisely, we focus on the trade-off between the extraction rate and its reliability, characterized by the optimal asymptotic speed at which the extraction error can be suppressed. We establish that the reliability of Gibbs-preserving operations and of thermal operations are respectively characterized by the Petz and the sandwiched Rényi relative entropies, demonstrating that the former in general strictly outperforms the latter, and providing new interpretations of several information-theoretic divergences. Our analysis reveals that operational constraints such as energy conservation impose stronger limitations on the achievable precision of quantum tasks than can be inferred from their asymptotic rates, thereby questioning the use of Gibbs-preserving operations as a mathematically convenient substitute for the physically realizable thermal processes.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that while Gibbs-preserving and thermal operations yield the same optimal work extraction rate (Helmholtz free energy), they differ significantly in reliability: Gibbs-preserving operations (characterized by Petz Rényi entropy) can suppress errors faster than thermal operations (characterized by sandwiched Rényi entropy), revealing that energy conservation imposes stricter precision limits beyond what asymptotic rates capture.
AI.motivation: Previous work suggested that both thermal operations and Gibbs-preserving operations yield the same optimal work extraction rate, making Gibbs-preserving operations seem a convenient mathematical substitute for physically realizable thermal processes. This paper challenges that equivalence by examining a more refined metric—the reliability or error suppression speed—rather than just the asymptotic rate.
AI.method: The authors analyze the trade-off between work extraction rate and reliability (error suppression speed) for both classes of operations. They characterize the optimal asymptotic error suppression speed using the Petz Rényi relative entropy (for Gibbs-preserving operations) and the sandwiched Rényi relative entropy (for thermal operations), then compare the two.
AI.result: The reliability of work extraction under Gibbs-preserving operations and thermal operations are respectively characterized by the Petz and sandwiched Rényi relative entropies. Gibbs-preserving operations generally achieve strictly faster error suppression (higher reliability) than thermal operations, meaning they outperform thermal operations in the precision-reliability trade-off.
AI.conclusion: Operational constraints like energy conservation impose stronger limitations on achievable precision than asymptotic rates suggest. Gibbs-preserving operations are not a physically faithful substitute for thermal operations when considering finite-resource or precision-critical scenarios. The findings also provide new interpretations of information-theoretic divergences in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Benchmarking Floquet Master Equations for Periodically Driven Open Quantum Systems
summary: The dynamics of open quantum systems is commonly described by quantum master equations derived under the assumption of weak system-bath coupling and a separation of timescales between system and bath. When the system is additionally subjected to a periodic driving, the validity of the resulting Floquet master equations is further restricted to regimes of weak or high-frequency driving. Here, we benchmark a set of commonly used Floquet master equations for a model of two locally driven spins coupled to a shared Ohmic reservoir at finite temperature. We systematically probe the accuracy of the equations as a function of the driving parameters, thus identifying limits of their applicability. Dynamical maps predicted by each master equation are compared against numerically exact non-Markovian simulations, tracking the full relaxation dynamics. We find that the accuracy of each master equation closely reflects the assumptions underlying its derivation. For the Floquet-Lindblad equation, errors can be strongly amplified near resonances where the secular approximation breaks down, while approaches that avoid the secular approximation perform better and exhibit a more systematic dependence of the error on driving frequency and amplitude.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks various Floquet master equations for open quantum systems under periodic driving, comparing them against numerically exact non-Markovian simulations for a model of two driven spins coupled to a shared Ohmic bath. The accuracy of each equation reflects its underlying assumptions, with secular-approximation-based equations failing near resonances, while non-secular approaches perform more robustly.
AI.motivation: To systematically benchmark the accuracy and identify the limits of validity of commonly used Floquet master equations for open quantum systems under periodic driving, by comparing them against exact non-Markovian simulations.
AI.method: Benchmarking a set of Floquet master equations against numerically exact non-Markovian simulations for a model of two locally driven spins coupled to a shared Ohmic reservoir at finite temperature, systematically probing accuracy as a function of driving parameters.
AI.result: The accuracy of each master equation closely reflects its derivation assumptions. The Floquet-Lindblad equation exhibits strongly amplified errors near resonances where the secular approximation breaks down, while non-secular approaches perform better with more systematic error dependence on driving frequency and amplitude.
AI.conclusion: Non-secular Floquet master equations are more reliable than secular-approximation-based ones, especially near resonances, and the choice of master equation should be guided by the driving parameter regime.

title: A framework for low-overhead quantum fault tolerance via spacetime lifting
summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computation is inherently a spacetime problem, requiring not merely good static quantum error-correcting codes but also low-overhead protocols for protecting and manipulating encoded quantum information over time. Fault complexes provide a homological framework for treating such protocols as single spacetime objects. In this work, we initiate the study of low-overhead fault complexes by introducing {spacetime lifting}, a method that constructs fault complexes from symmetry-reduced product structures beyond standard foliation. We show that spacetime lifting yields fault complexes and in particular {spacetime-lifted} memory experiments with almost-linear fault distance in the total spacetime cost, which substantially outperforms existing constructions. We further interpret fault complexes as measurement-based cluster-state protocols and identify general conditions under which they realize fault-tolerant logical teleportation, showing that spacetime-lifted constructions combine favorable scaling with operational schemes. Our study opens a path toward more efficient quantum fault tolerance through general complex constructions.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces "spacetime lifting," a method for constructing fault complexes (spacetime objects encoding fault-tolerant quantum protocols) from symmetry-reduced product structures. It yields fault-tolerant memory experiments with almost-linear fault distance in total spacetime cost—outperforming existing constructions—and interprets these as measurement-based cluster-state protocols realizing fault-tolerant logical teleportation.
AI.motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires not only good static quantum error-correcting codes but also low-overhead protocols for protecting and manipulating encoded quantum information over time. Existing approaches lack a unified spacetime framework that yields favorable scaling.
AI.method: The paper introduces "spacetime lifting," which constructs fault complexes from symmetry-reduced product structures beyond standard foliation. Fault complexes are treated as single homological spacetime objects encoding fault-tolerant protocols.

The fault complexes are interpreted as measurement-based cluster-state protocols, and conditions for fault-tolerant logical teleportation are identified.

title: Robustness of Entanglement Manipulation for almost i.i.d. sources
summary: We study the robustness of asymptotic entanglement manipulation beyond the exact i.i.d. regime, focusing on Mazzola--Sutter--Renner (MSR) almost i.i.d. sources, which allow a sublinear number of deviations from a tensor-power structure. For pure MSR sources along a bipartite reference state $|φ\rangle_{AB}$, we prove that the entanglement concentration rate is robust: every rate below the entropy of entanglement $S(φ_A)$ remains achievable. Moreover, this can be done by a single Schur--Weyl concentration protocol that is universal within the MSR class, depending only on the reference state and not on the particular source sequence. For mixed MSR sources along a reference state $ρ_{AB}$, we prove a source-dependent entanglement-distillation achievability result: every rate below the coherent information $I(A\rangle B)_ρ$ of the reference state is achievable, although the entanglement distillation protocol may depend on the particular MSR source sequence. For the reverse task of entanglement dilution, we prove a rate-robustness theorem: the asymptotic entanglement cost of any MSR target sequence along $ρ_{AB}$ is at most $E_F^\infty(ρ_{AB})$, the regularized entanglement of formation of the reference state. To establish these results, we prove structural and entropic properties of MSR almost i.i.d. sequences which may be useful in other information-theoretic settings. Thus, for the achievability statements considered here, MSR almost i.i.d. perturbations exhibit the same asymptotic behaviour as their i.i.d. reference states, despite allowing sublinear deviations from a tensor-power structure.

AI.tldr: The paper studies entanglement manipulation beyond exact i.i.d. settings, using MSR almost i.i.d. sources (allowing sublinear deviations from tensor-power structure). For pure bipartite states, entanglement concentration rates are robust (any rate below entropy of entanglement is achievable via a universal protocol). For mixed states, source-dependent distillation achieves rates below coherent information. For entanglement dilution, cost is bounded by regularized entanglement of formation. Overall, MSR perturbations preserve asymptotic i.i.d. behavior for these achievability tasks.
AI.motivation: To understand whether asymptotic entanglement manipulation protocols remain robust when the source deviates from the ideal i.i.d. (independent and identically distributed) assumption, allowing sublinear deviations from a tensor-power structure as captured by MSR almost i.i.d. sources.
AI.method: The authors analyze MSR almost i.i.d. sequences, deriving structural and entropic properties. They employ Schur–Weyl concentration protocols for pure states and source-dependent distillation protocols for mixed states. Entanglement dilution bounds are established via analysis of regularized entanglement of formation.
AI.result: For pure MSR sources: entanglement concentration rate is robust — every rate below $S(φ_A)$ is achievable via a universal Schur–Weyl protocol. For mixed MSR sources: every rate below $I(A\rangle B)_ρ$ is achievable with source-dependent distillation. For dilution: entanglement cost is at most $E_F^\infty(ρ_{AB})$. MSR perturbations exhibit same asymptotic behavior as i.i.d. reference states.
AI.conclusion: MSR almost i.i.d. perturbations preserve the asymptotic entanglement manipulation rates of their i.i.d. reference states for the achievability tasks considered, demonstrating robustness of entanglement theory beyond the exact i.i.d. regime.

title: Nanostructure modelling with early fault tolerant quantum computers
summary: Semiconductor nanostructures are central to many developing technologies. Notably, double quantum dots are especially important for semiconductor spin-qubit architectures, quantum sensing applications, and quantum-dot solar cells. Accurate modelling is highly desirable but conventional methods can struggle when dynamics involve more than two interacting electrons. In this work, we present a quantum simulation framework capable of addressing multi-electron double quantum dots. We adopt an efficiently scaling 1$^\text{st}$ quantised representation of the system and develop algorithms based on both Trotterisation and qubitisation. Incorporating insights from classical simulations enables us to produce resource estimates that are more realistic than those obtained from theoretical error bounds. Using a standard surface code model with physical noise at $10^{-3}$, our results indicate that the ground-state energy of four electrons in a double quantum dot can be estimated in approximately 24 hours using 226k physical qubits, or an eight-electron system in 3.4 days with 314k qubits (with runtimes falling dramatically when more qubits are available). We anticipate that incorporating very recent advances including dense surface code architectures (Low et al. arXiv:2605.30455) may reduce these costs significantly further. We conclude that early fault tolerant computers may prove to be valuable tools for designing mature-era quantum technologies.

AI.method: The authors adopt a 1st quantised representation of the system and develop algorithms based on both Trotterisation and qubitisation, incorporating insights from classical simulations to produce more realistic resource estimates than theoretical error bounds.
AI.result: Using a standard surface code model with physical noise at 10⁻³, the ground-state energy of four electrons in a double quantum dot can be estimated in ~24 hours using 226k physical qubits, or an eight-electron system in 3.4 days with 314k qubits, with runtimes falling dramatically when more qubits are available.

title: Energy-Modulated Time-Asymmetric Spontaneous Collapse: Forward-Backward Dynamics from Stochastic Ito Reversal and Bright Solitons
summary: We present a rigorous theoretical framework for symmetry breaking and quantum irreversibility arising from stochastic Ito field reversal within a cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrodinger equation (CQ-NLSE) formalism. Starting from three physically motivated considerations, forward and backward nonlinear stochastic differential equations are derived via the Ito calculus. Kinematic time-reversal is shown to be fundamentally incompatible with the Ito stochastic structure, yielding the universal asymmetry-coupling parameter of 2/3. An energy-driven collapse operator proportional to the product of noise strength, local probability density, and excitation energy squared is introduced, amplifying the collapse in high-density, high-excitation regions. Exactly bright soliton solutions are obtained for a quasi-one-dimensional BEC of attractive Li-7 atoms, with forward and backward amplitude ratio of 1.870. Heat map analysis of the parameter planes reveals that the forward collapse operator grows monotonically in time while the backward counterpart decays, achieving a ratio approximately 1030, sharply distinguishing this framework from conventional symmetric collapse models.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for symmetry breaking and quantum irreversibility using stochastic Itô field reversal in a cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, yielding a universal 2/3 asymmetry-coupling parameter and demonstrating irreversible collapse dynamics with forward-to-backward amplitude ratio ~1030.
AI.motivation: To rigorously establish the incompatibility of kinematic time-reversal with Itô stochastic structure and derive universal symmetry breaking from first principles in nonlinear quantum systems.
AI.method: Stochastic Itô calculus is used to derive forward and backward nonlinear stochastic differential equations from three physically motivated considerations. An energy-driven collapse operator proportional to noise strength × local probability density × excitation energy squared is introduced. Exact bright soliton solutions are obtained for quasi-1D BEC of attractive Li-7 atoms.
AI.result: Universal asymmetry-coupling parameter of 2/3; forward-to-backward amplitude ratio of 1.870 for bright solitons; forward collapse operator grows monotonically while backward decays, yielding ratio ~1030, sharply distinct from symmetric collapse models.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a sharp distinction from conventional symmetric collapse models and establishes fundamental quantum irreversibility arising from stochastic Itô structure.

title: Breakeven demonstration of quantum low-density parity-check codes
summary: High-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes are a leading candidate for fault-tolerant quantum computing. They feature higher encoding rates than planar alternatives such as the surface code, but their implementation often entails significant hardware hurdles like the need for long-range couplers. We leverage the flexibility of a trapped-ion quantum computer to demonstrate nine quantum error-correcting codes with starkly different qubit connectivity requirements on a single device without any hardware reconfiguration. These experiments span three families of quantum error-correcting codes: qLDPC codes, topological codes, and concatenated codes. With a qLDPC code encoding 4 logical qubits into 18 physical qubits, we achieve a logical error rate up to $9\times$ better than a previous demonstration of a similar code on superconducting solid-state qubits. Moreover, our implementation exhibits breakeven performance, with some instances achieving qubit lifetimes comparable to or slightly exceeding that of our trapped-ion qubits. We use a novel implementation of the optical-metastable-ground (OMG) architecture for addressable mid-circuit measurement and reset, which enables us to perform these experiments without any ion transport or dedicated coolant ions, requirements that typically consume a large fraction of the runtime or ion count of trapped-ion quantum computers.

AI.tldr: Trapped-ion quantum computer demonstrates 9 quantum error-correcting codes (qLDPC, topological, concatenated) without hardware reconfiguration, achieving up to 9× better logical error rate than previous superconducting qLDPC implementations and breakeven qubit lifetimes, enabled by a novel optical-metastable-ground (OMG) architecture for mid-circuit measurement and reset without ion transport or coolant ions.
AI.motivation: High-rate qLDPC codes offer superior encoding rates over planar codes like the surface code but pose hardware challenges such as long-range couplers. Additionally, trapped-ion quantum computers typically require ion transport or dedicated coolant ions for mid-circuit operations, consuming significant runtime or ion resources.
AI.method: Leveraged a single trapped-ion device to run 9 quantum error-correcting codes from three families (qLDPC, topological, concatenated) without hardware reconfiguration, using a novel optical-metastable-ground (OMG) architecture for addressable mid-circuit measurement and reset.
AI.result: Achieved up to 9× better logical error rate than a previous superconducting qLDPC demonstration for a code encoding 4 logical qubits into 18 physical qubits. Demonstrated breakeven performance with qubit lifetimes comparable to or slightly exceeding physical qubit lifetimes.
AI.conclusion: Trapped-ion platforms offer unique flexibility for implementing diverse QEC codes, including those requiring complex connectivity like qLDPC codes, without hardware reconfiguration, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum element-wise transforms
summary: Quantum algorithms for basic numerical linear algebraic tasks have proven essential for translating diverse problems to a unified quantum computational context. Many of these tasks -- e.g., applying a polynomial function to the spectrum of a matrix embedded in a unitary process (a so-called block encoding), or taking linear combinations of block encodings -- are well-addressed by techniques like quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) or linear combination of unitaries (LCU). However, there exist useful matrix transforms whose realization by existing quantum algorithms is unclear or inefficient. In this work we construct improved quantum algorithms for some of these transforms, the simplest of which is a polynomial function applied element-wise. We show the space required to compute quantum element-wise transforms can be reduced exponentially in the degree of the applied function compared to prior work, and raise and rectify errors in previous constructions. We present our algorithms alongside applications to machine learning, simulation, and signal processing.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces improved quantum algorithms for element-wise polynomial transforms of matrices, achieving exponential reduction in space complexity relative to prior work, with applications in machine learning, simulation, and signal processing.
AI.motivation: While QSVT and LCU handle many numerical linear algebra tasks well, certain useful matrix transforms (e.g., element-wise polynomial functions) are not efficiently realized by existing quantum algorithms.
AI.method: The authors construct improved quantum algorithms for element-wise polynomial transforms, reducing the required space exponentially in the degree of the applied function compared to prior work, and correcting errors in previous constructions.
AI.result: Exponential reduction in space complexity (in the degree of the applied polynomial) for quantum element-wise transforms; errors in prior work are identified and rectified.
AI.conclusion: The proposed algorithms fill a gap in quantum numerical linear algebra capabilities and are applicable to machine learning, simulation, and signal processing.
